title: Time on a work order in the last 90 days turns Technician on
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in to production (the live app, app.shopview.com) as an Admin of the production test account, at its test location, Trucks Hill 2.
  • Shortly before the release reached production, have a new staff member for this test on production, staff member A, active, on the built-in Parts Manager role, with Time Clock on, Billable set to No, enrolled at Trucks Hill 2, whose only work is one time entry on a work order that started 30 days before the release (written down with a screenshot of the staff record).
custom_steps:
1. Open Settings, Staff.
  2. Open staff member A's Edit Staff Member window.
  3. Open Work Orders, Board View, at Trucks Hill 2.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Staff member A's row shows "Yes" in the Technician column.

Step 2:

  • Technician is on.

Step 3:

  • Staff member A has a column.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 20 (3 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11884 (Story 6, Release day)

  • S6-R1: “Technician is turned on for each staff member whose user is active, whose Time Clock is on and who has a role other than the built-in Office User or Time Clock User role, when they meet any of these, at any location of their organization:”
  • S6-R1 (a): “(a) has a time entry on a work order, part sales included, whose start is no more than 90 days (to the second) before the moment the release step runs, or later, including manual entries made by someone else (time on a department alone does not count; an entry that has both a department and a work order counts as time on the work order);”
  • Key Decisions: “Release day keeps every shop as it is: Technician is turned on per person, from evidence.”
  • Goals: “On release day no shop loses a technician: everyone who appeared as a technician the day before and did technician work in the last 90 days still appears.”
  • Goals: “Existing shops need no setup: release day sets the toggle from recent work. New staff on the built-in Technician or Foreman role start on; everyone else starts off, so a parts or office hire never lands on the board by accident.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

AUTOMATION: HOLD - needs the before values taken on production shortly before the release reaches production; run on production after the release
